subject: System Design
title: WhatsApp's Message Delivery
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on WhatsApp's Message Delivery.

hook.text: WhatsApp delivers 100 billion messages per day to 2 billion users. With a team of just 50 engineers at its peak.

buildup.text: WhatsApp uses Erlang — a language designed for telecom. It handles millions of concurrent connections per server.

discovery.text: Messages are stored temporarily until delivered. Once both blue check marks appear, the server deletes the message.

twist.text: End-to-end encryption means WhatsApp can't read your messages. The server is just a relay — it never sees the content.

climax.text: WhatsApp's design philosophy: minimal server state, maximum efficiency. Fewer servers means less to manage.

punchline.text: Store nothing, relay everything — minimal state, maximum scale.

quiz.question: Why does WhatsApp delete messages after delivery?
options: To minimize server state and storage requirements
To protect user privacy by law
